question: Should OpenClaw accept the new trusted disabled-plugin recovery capability and generic setup/catalog seams as the permanent host boundary for Signal’s shipped-config migration?
rationale: The patch deliberately expands the conditions under which a disabled plugin owner may be loaded during invalid-config recovery and adds public plugin/setup metadata; code review can assess mechanics, but maintainers must choose the long-term security and compatibility contract.

options.title: Approve the bounded recovery contract
options.body: Accept the capability only when the final review confirms trusted official provenance, exact channel scoping, and inert handling for all other disabled owners.

options.title: Keep recovery owner-specific
options.body: Require Signal to use an existing owner-local recovery path and avoid adding the generic metadata and loader behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded recovery contract
recommendation.body: Accept the capability only when the final review confirms trusted official provenance, exact channel scoping, and inert handling for all other disabled owners.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch history shows the strongest available connection to the proposed Signal migration and recovery boundary.
